subject: Re: Cryptographic shadowing & revocation paths — acceptance criteria and runbook
messages:
From: Samantha Ruiz <sruiz@healthtech.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Green <alex.green@healthtech.com>

Subject: Initial: BYOK revocation and shadowing questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment checklist yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security team about BYOK revocation scenarios: specifically they want to understand the 'shadowing' approach you mentioned — keeping a non-useful but verifiable record of prior keys so that we can demonstrate non-replay during audits. They also asked for a clear revocation path (what you called the revocation 'forwarding' or roll-forward model) that works even when the on-prem HSM is air-gapped for short windows.

Attached is a small CSV with our current key reference map and a sample of our egress telemetry (egress-telemetry-sample.log). Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood supports a shadow index that is cryptographically unlinkable to live keys but auditable?
- How revocation propagation works when the HSM is temporarily offline and the control plane needs to mark keys revoked for routing decisions?
- Any recommended runbook steps for emergency operator-initiated rotation + revocation (we need a prescriptive checklist for our auditors).

Appreciate the help — our timeline for the conformance audit is the end of the quarter.

Samantha
Security Lead, HealthTech Diagnostics
From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-05T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial: BYOK revocation and shadowing questions

Folks — forwarding HealthTech's questions. They want an explanation + a short runbook we can hand them. High-level constraints: their HSM may be air-gapped for maintenance windows (~15–45m), they require an auditable (but unlinkable) shadow index for prior keys, and they want a deterministic revocation propagation that doesn't rely solely on live HSM connectivity.

My proposal below (draft) — feel free to correct and expand. If this looks good, I'll send to Samantha with attachments and a request to schedule a 30-min runbook dry-run.

--- Draft proposal (internal) ---
1) Shadowing model: create a shadow index record for each key epoch consisting of {epoch_id, salt, hash(commitment)} where commitment = HMAC_SHA256(salt || public_key_fingerprint) performed by the attestation service. The salt is stored only in Redwood control plane (encrypted at rest) and the commitment cannot be reversed to the public key without the salt. HealthTech can keep the list of commitments and we can provide a signed attestation of the salt for audit windows. This provides an auditable list without exposing linkability.

2) Revocation propagation: introduce a 'revocation ledger' that accepts signed revocation transactions. Replication model: when HSM is offline, operator issues a signed offline-revocation blob which the on-prem proxy holds; once control-plane connectivity is restored, the proxy posts the blob into the ledger and the ledger returns a revocation-epoch confirmation. Routing decisions in the serving plane consult a local cache seeded from the ledger; cache invalidation is TTL-based but forced by the revocation-epoch confirmation.

3) Emergency runbook (summary):
- Step A: Operator initiates local emergency-rotation on HSM (generate new key pair, seal, produce audit log).
- Step B: Operator creates signed offline-revocation blob and distributes to designated proxies (use out-of-band MFA for signing).
- Step C: When connectivity restores, post blob to ledger and verify revocation-epoch confirmation.
- Step D: Validate client routing configs and egress telemetry for any calls tied to old key epochs; run attestations and produce report.

4) Telemetry / evidence: we can produce a signed timeline (log of attestations + ledger confirmations) and provide sample egress telemetry that maps to key epochs for auditors.

Open questions:
- How do we manage salt escrow for long-term audits? (Recommend seeded escrow with a KMS-wrapped keyshare split across the customer and Redwood legal escrow).
- Do we want operator-eviction flows (zeroize) automated for key compromise? (I think yes; propose one-click zeroize in private console tied to multi-sig operator approvals)

Ben / Karthik — technical review and notes please.

Thanks,
Naomi
Sr. Security PM — Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-05T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial: BYOK revocation and shadowing questions

Naomi — good draft. A few technical clarifications and constraints from the infra/runtime side:

1) Commitment construction: HMAC(salt||fingerprint) is fine; recommend using an attested enclave to sign commitments so the audit attestation includes enclave measurement. We'll add an 'attestation bundle' output that HealthTech can verify offline against a published public key.

2) Revocation ledger: prefer a compact signed Merkle-append-only log (not a full blockchain) so we can provide succinct proofs of inclusion for auditor queries. The on-prem proxy will store the latest root and a set of pending blobs. When the proxy posts a blob it receives a signed inclusion proof. Serving nodes validate inclusion proofs against their cached root; this keeps per-request costs low.

3) Offline-revocation blob design: must include operator identity, expiration window, and an integrity HMAC. Recommend also packing a pre-image of the salt-holder proof so that once posted, the ledger records the epoch transition deterministically.

4) Cache invalidation: TTL is insufficient for critical revocations. We'll implement a 'revocation-epoch' monotonic counter; serving nodes will reject tokens signed under older epoch numbers when the local epoch > token epoch. The epoch advancement occurs when ledger inclusion proof is applied. This allows immediate logical revocation for routing without waiting for TTL expiry.

5) Network / egress notes: proxies must be able to post blobs via a tightly-scoped egress route to the control plane. For air-gapped windows we need an alternate poster (jump host with storage) — recommend a signed S3-like drop with time-limited credentials that the control plane polls when network returns.

I'll draft the exact blob JSON and a minimal Merkle log API.

-karthik
Lead Infra Engineer
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-05T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial: BYOK revocation and shadowing questions

Thanks both — these are solid. A couple of pragmatic additions before we send back to HealthTech:

- Runbook dry-run: propose scheduling a 30-minute drill with HealthTech ops next Tue (2025-12-09) where we exercise creating an offline-revocation blob and posting it. I'll own the checklist and provide a small script for the proxy to generate the blob.

- Escrow: for long-term audits let's avoid moving customer salts to our custody. Instead offer a dual-escrow model: Redwood holds an encrypted share (wrapped with our KMS), customer holds the second share. To produce evidence we combine shares using an MPC service that reveals only the salt commitment necessary for the auditor's narrow window. We'll document the legal/access controls.

- Evidence packaging: we'll provide HealthTech a signed 'audit bundle' (revocation ledger inclusion proofs, attestation bundles, and egress timeline) in a tarball and a short checklist of what to present to auditors.

Naomi — go ahead and send to Samantha with the attachments and propose the 12/09 dry-run. I'll prepare the proxy script and the initial Merkle API docs (link in related_links once ready).

-ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
